problems.title: Sum of Array Elements
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums`, return the sum of all its elements.

An empty array has sum `0`. Use a loop and an accumulator rather than a built-in reducer.

problems.title: Largest Element in an Array
problems.statementMd: Given a non-empty integer array `nums`, return its largest element **without** using `Math.max` or sorting.

problems.title: Count Even Numbers
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums`, return how many of its elements are even.

Zero and negative even numbers count as even.

problems.title: Linear Search
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`, return the **first** index where `target` appears, or `-1` if it is absent.

problems.title: Smallest Element in an Array
problems.statementMd: Given a non-empty integer array `nums`, return its smallest element **without** using `Math.min` or sorting.

problems.title: Count Elements Greater Than X
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `x`, return how many elements are **strictly greater** than `x`.

problems.title: Sum of Elements Greater Than X
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `x`, return the sum of all elements **strictly greater** than `x`. Return `0` if none qualify.

problems.title: Reverse an Array
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return a **new** array with the elements in reverse order. Build it with a loop instead of `reverse()`, and leave `nums` unchanged.

problems.title: Keep Only Positive Numbers
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return a new array containing only its **positive** numbers (greater than 0), in their original order. Don't use `Array.filter`.

problems.title: Check if an Array is Sorted
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if it is sorted in **non-decreasing** order (each element is at least the one before it), otherwise `false`.

problems.title: Second Largest Element
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums`, return the **second largest distinct** value. If there is no such value (fewer than two distinct values), return `null`.

Try to do it in one pass without sorting.

problems.title: Sum of Elements at Odd Indexes
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return the sum of the elements at **odd indexes** (1, 3, 5, ...). Indexes start at 0.

problems.title: Last Occurrence of a Target
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`, return the **last** index where `target` appears, or `-1` if it is absent.

problems.title: Count Positives, Negatives and Zeroes
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `[positives, negatives, zeroes]` with how many elements are greater than 0, less than 0, and equal to 0.

problems.title: Difference Between Largest and Smallest
problems.statementMd: Given a non-empty integer array `nums`, return `max - min`, the difference between its largest and smallest elements.

problems.title: Sum of Elements at Even Indexes
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return the sum of the elements at **even indexes** (0, 2, 4, ...). Indexes start at 0.

problems.title: Replace Negatives with Zero
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, replace every negative number with `0` **in the same array**. Don't return anything; the array itself is checked.

problems.title: Rotate an Array Right by One
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, rotate it **right** by one position in place: the last element moves to the front and every other element shifts one step right. Don't return anything.

problems.title: Left Rotate an Array by One
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, rotate it **left** by one position in place: the first element moves to the end and every other element shifts one step left. Don't return anything.

problems.title: Append One Array to Another
problems.statementMd: Given two integer arrays `a` and `b`, return a new array with all of `a` followed by all of `b`. Build it with loops instead of `concat` or the spread operator.

problems.title: Check if Two Arrays are Equal
problems.statementMd: Given two integer arrays `a` and `b`, return `true` only if they have the same length and the same values in the same order.

problems.title: Check if an Array is a Palindrome
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if it reads the same from both ends (for example `[1, 2, 1]`), otherwise `false`.

Try it with two pointers, one at each end, moving toward the middle.

problems.title: Reverse an Array In Place
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, reverse it **in place** using two pointers, one starting at each end. Don't create a second array and don't return anything.

problems.title: Frequency of Every Number
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return a plain object that maps each distinct value to how many times it appears. For example `[1, 2, 1]` gives `{ "1": 2, "2": 1 }` (object keys are strings; key order doesn't matter).

problems.title: Unique Intersection of Two Arrays
problems.statementMd: Given two integer arrays `a` and `b`, return the values that appear in **both**, each value once. The order of the result doesn't matter.

problems.title: Intersection of Two Arrays with Counts
problems.statementMd: Given two integer arrays `a` and `b`, return their intersection **including duplicates**: a value appears in the result as many times as it appears in both arrays (the smaller of its two counts). The order of the result doesn't matter.

problems.title: First Element that Appears Exactly Once
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return the **first** element (from the left) that appears exactly once in the whole array. If no element is unique, return `null`.

problems.title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the maximum sum of any **contiguous** subarray of exactly `k` elements.

problems.title: Minimum Sum Subarray of Size K
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the minimum sum of any **contiguous** subarray of exactly `k` elements.

problems.title: Most Even Numbers in a Window of Size K
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the largest number of **even** values contained in any contiguous window of exactly `k` elements.

problems.title: Windows of Size K with a Target Sum
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, an integer `k` and an integer `target`, return the starting indexes (in increasing order) of every contiguous window of exactly `k` elements whose sum equals `target`.

problems.title: Longest Subarray with Sum at Most K
problems.statementMd: Given an array of **positive** integers `nums` and an integer `k`, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is **at most** `k`. Return `0` if no single element fits.

problems.title: Longest Subarray with at Most K Odd Numbers
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray containing **at most** `k` odd numbers.

problems.title: Range Sum Queries with a Prefix Array
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums` and a list of `queries`, where each query is `[left, right]` (0-based, inclusive), return an array with the sum of `nums[left..right]` for each query.

Build a prefix-sum array once so each query is answered in O(1).

problems.title: Unique Triplets with a Target Sum
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`, return all **unique** triplets of values `[a, b, c]` taken from three different positions such that `a + b + c == target`. Triplets are unique by their values; the order of triplets and of values inside a triplet doesn't matter.

problems.title: Sum of Array Elements (Recursion)
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return the sum of its elements **using recursion** instead of a loop: the sum of an array is its first element plus the sum of the rest, and an empty array sums to `0`.

problems.title: Reverse an Array (Recursion)
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return a new array with its elements reversed, **using recursion**: swap the outer pair, then reverse what's left in between.

problems.title: Check if Array Is Sorted and Rotated
Pattern 1: Square of Stars
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Every one of the `n` rows has `n` stars. For `n = 3`: `***`, `***`, `***`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 2: Right-Angled Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (1-based) has `i` stars. For `n = 3`: `*`, `**`, `***`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 3: Right-Angled Number Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` is the numbers `1` to `i` written together. For `n = 3`: `1`, `12`, `123`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 4: Repeated Number Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` is the number `i` written `i` times. For `n = 3`: `1`, `22`, `333`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 5: Inverted Right Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (1-based) has `n - i + 1` stars. For `n = 3`: `***`, `**`, `*`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 6: Inverted Number Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` is the numbers `1` to `n - i + 1` written together. For `n = 3`: `123`, `12`, `1`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 7: Star Pyramid
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (1-based) has `n - i` leading spaces followed by `2i - 1` stars. For `n = 3`: `  *`, ` ***`, `*****`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 8: Inverted Star Pyramid
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (0-based) has `i` leading spaces followed by `2(n - i) - 1` stars. For `n = 3`: `*****`, ` ***`, `  *`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 9: Diamond
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

The star pyramid for `n` (pattern 7) followed by the inverted star pyramid for `n` (pattern 8), so `2n` rows in total. The widest row appears twice.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 10: Half Diamond
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

`2n - 1` rows. Row `i` (1-based) has `i` stars while `i <= n`, then `2n - i` stars. For `n = 3`: `*`, `**`, `***`, `**`, `*`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 11: Binary Number Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (0-based) has `i + 1` digits that alternate between `1` and `0`. Even rows start with `1`, odd rows with `0`. For `n = 4`: `1`, `01`, `101`, `0101`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 12: Number Crown
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (1-based) is `1..i`, then `2(n - i)` spaces, then `i..1`. For `n = 3`: `1    1`, `12  21`, `123321`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 13: Increasing Number Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` has `i` numbers, continuing a single count that starts at `1`, separated by single spaces. For `n = 3`: `1`, `2 3`, `4 5 6`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 14: Increasing Letter Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` is the first `i` capital letters. For `n = 3`: `A`, `AB`, `ABC`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 15: Reverse Letter Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (1-based) is the first `n - i + 1` capital letters. For `n = 3`: `ABC`, `AB`, `A`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 16: Alpha Ramp
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (1-based) is the `i`-th capital letter written `i` times. For `n = 3`: `A`, `BB`, `CCC`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 17: Alpha Hill
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (1-based) has `n - i` leading spaces, then the letters from `A` up to the `i`-th letter and back down to `A`. For `n = 3`: `  A`, ` ABA`, `ABCBA`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 18: Alpha Triangle
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

Row `i` (1-based) holds the last `i` letters of the first `n` capital letters, in order, separated by single spaces. For `n = 3`: `C`, `B C`, `A B C`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 19: Symmetric Void
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

`2n` rows. The top half, for `i = 0..n-1`, is `n - i` stars, `2i` spaces, `n - i` stars. The bottom half, for `i = 1..n`, is `i` stars, `2(n - i)` spaces, `i` stars. For `n = 2`: `****`, `*  *`, `*  *`, `****`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 20: Symmetric Butterfly
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

`2n - 1` rows. Row `i` (1-based) has `s` stars, `2(n - s)` spaces and `s` stars, where `s = i` for `i <= n` and `s = 2n - i` after that. For `n = 2`: `*  *`, `****`, `*  *`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 21: Hollow Square
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

An `n` by `n` square whose border is stars and whose inside is spaces. For `n = 3`: `***`, `* *`, `***`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Pattern 22: The Number Pattern
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer `n`, build the pattern below and return it as an array of strings, one string per printed row.

A `(2n - 1)` by `(2n - 1)` grid of digits written together. Each cell holds `n` minus its distance to the nearest edge, so the border is `n` and the centre is `1`. For `n = 2`: `222`, `212`, `222`.

Rows have **no trailing spaces**. Leading spaces are part of the row.

problems.title: Count All Digits of a Number
problems.statementMd:
Given a non-negative integer `n`, return how many digits it has. `0` has one digit.

Use arithmetic (`% 10` and integer division) rather than converting to a string.

problems.title: Count Odd Digits in a Number
problems.statementMd: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return how many of its digits are odd.

problems.title: Largest Digit in a Number
problems.statementMd: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return its largest digit.

problems.title: Factorial of a Number
problems.statementMd: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return `n!` (the product `1 * 2 * ... * n`). By definition `0! = 1`.

problems.title: Armstrong Number
problems.statementMd:
A positive integer with `k` digits is an **Armstrong number** when the sum of each digit raised to the power `k` equals the number itself. For example `153 = 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3`.

Given `n`, return `true` if it is an Armstrong number, otherwise `false`.

problems.title: Check for Prime Number
problems.statementMd: Given an integer `n`, return `true` if it is prime (greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and itself), otherwise `false`.

problems.title: GCD of Two Numbers
problems.statementMd: Given two positive integers `a` and `b`, return their greatest common divisor: the largest integer that divides both.

problems.title: LCM of Two Numbers
problems.statementMd: Given two positive integers `a` and `b`, return their least common multiple: the smallest positive integer divisible by both.

problems.title: Divisors of a Number
problems.statementMd: Given a positive integer `n`, return all of its divisors in increasing order.

problems.title: Count Odd Numbers in an Array
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return how many of its elements are odd. Negative numbers can be odd too.

problems.title: Second Highest Occurring Element
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, find the element whose frequency is the **second highest distinct frequency** in the array. If several elements share that frequency, return the smallest of them. If every element has the same frequency, return `-1`.

problems.title: Sum of Highest and Lowest Frequency
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return the sum of the highest frequency and the lowest frequency of any element in it.

problems.title: Sum of First N Numbers (Recursion)
problems.statementMd: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return `1 + 2 + ... + n` using **recursion** (no loop and no formula). The sum for `n = 0` is `0`.

problems.title: Factorial of a Number (Recursion)
problems.statementMd: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return `n!` using **recursion**: `n! = n * (n - 1)!` and `0! = 1`.

problems.title: Check if a Number is Prime (Recursion)
problems.statementMd: Given an integer `n`, return `true` if it is prime, otherwise `false`. Try writing the divisor check as a **recursive** helper `check(n, i)` that tests divisor `i` and recurses on `i + 1` while `i * i <= n`.

problems.title: Sum of Digits (Recursion)
problems.statementMd: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return the sum of its digits. Try solving it **recursively**: the digit sum of `n` is its last digit plus the digit sum of the rest.

problems.title: Selection Sort
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums`, sort it in non-decreasing order with **selection sort** and return it.

Selection sort repeatedly finds the minimum of the unsorted part and swaps it to the front of that part. Don't call the built-in `sort`.

problems.title: Bubble Sort
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums`, sort it in non-decreasing order with **bubble sort** and return it.

Bubble sort repeatedly swaps adjacent elements that are out of order, so the largest remaining value bubbles to the end on each pass. Stop early when a pass makes no swap.

problems.title: Insertion Sort
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums`, sort it in non-decreasing order with **insertion sort** and return it.

Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix: each new element is shifted left until it sits after a value that isn't larger.

problems.title: Merge Sort
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums`, sort it in non-decreasing order with **merge sort** and return it.

Merge sort splits the array in half, sorts each half recursively and merges the two sorted halves.

problems.title: Quick Sort
problems.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums`, sort it in non-decreasing order with **quick sort** and return it.

Quick sort picks a pivot, partitions the array so smaller values come before it and larger ones after, then sorts both sides recursively.

problems.title: Recursive Bubble Sort
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, sort it in non-decreasing order with **bubble sort written recursively** and return it: one pass of adjacent swaps moves the largest value to the end, then the function calls itself on the first `n - 1` elements.

problems.title: Recursive Insertion Sort
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, sort it in non-decreasing order with **insertion sort written recursively** and return it: sort the first `n - 1` elements recursively, then insert the last element into place.

problems.title: Union of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.statementMd: Given two sorted integer arrays `a` and `b` (they may contain duplicates), return their **union**: every distinct value that appears in either array, in increasing order.

problems.title: Intersection of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.statementMd: Given two sorted integer arrays `a` and `b`, return their **intersection** in increasing order. A value that appears `p` times in `a` and `q` times in `b` appears `min(p, q)` times in the answer.

problems.title: Leaders in an Array
problems.statementMd:
An element is a **leader** if it is strictly greater than every element to its right. The last element is always a leader.

Given an integer array `nums`, return all leaders in the order they appear in `nums`.

problems.title: Find the Repeating and Missing Number
problems.statementMd:
You're given an array `nums` of size `n` holding values from `1` to `n`. Exactly one value appears twice and exactly one value is missing.

Return `[repeating, missing]`.

problems.title: Count Inversions
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return the number of **inversions**: pairs of indexes `(i, j)` with `i < j` and `nums[i] > nums[j]`.

problems.title: Longest Subarray with Sum K
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` (values may be negative) and an integer `k`, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is exactly `k`, or `0` if there is none.

problems.title: Largest Subarray with Sum 0
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose elements sum to `0`, or `0` if there is none.

problems.title: Count Subarrays with XOR K
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the number of contiguous subarrays whose bitwise XOR equals `k`.

problems.title: Lower Bound
problems.statementMd: Given a sorted array `nums` and a value `x`, return the **lower bound** of `x`: the smallest index `i` with `nums[i] >= x`. If every element is smaller than `x`, return `nums.length`.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

problems.title: Upper Bound
problems.statementMd: Given a sorted array `nums` and a value `x`, return the **upper bound** of `x`: the smallest index `i` with `nums[i] > x`. If no element is greater than `x`, return `nums.length`.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

problems.title: Floor and Ceil in a Sorted Array
problems.statementMd: Given a sorted array `nums` and a value `x`, return `[floor, ceil]`, where the floor is the largest element `<= x` and the ceil is the smallest element `>= x`. Use `-1` for one that doesn't exist.

problems.title: How Many Times Is the Array Rotated
problems.statementMd: An array of **distinct** integers was sorted in increasing order and then rotated right some number of times. Given the rotated array `nums`, return how many times it was rotated (equivalently, the index of its smallest element).

problems.title: Count Occurrences in a Sorted Array
problems.statementMd: Given a sorted integer array `nums` and a value `x`, return how many times `x` occurs in `nums`, in `O(log n)` time.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

problems.title: Nth Root of a Number
problems.statementMd: Given two positive integers `n` and `m`, return the integer `x` with `x^n = m`. If no integer works, return `-1`.

problems.title: Aggressive Cows
problems.statementMd: You're given the positions of `stalls` along a line (distinct, unsorted) and `k` cows. Place the cows in stalls so that the **minimum distance** between any two cows is as large as possible, and return that distance.

problems.title: K-th Element of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.statementMd: Given two sorted arrays `a` and `b` and an integer `k`, return the `k`-th smallest element (1-based) of the combined sorted array, without merging the arrays.

problems.title: Minimise Max Distance to Gas Station
problems.statementMd: Gas stations stand at sorted integer positions `arr`. You may add `k` new stations anywhere (not necessarily at integer positions). Return the smallest possible value of the **largest distance between adjacent stations**, rounded to 2 decimal places (as a number).

problems.title: Row with Maximum 1s
problems.statementMd: Given an `n x m` binary matrix `mat` in which every row is sorted (all `0`s before all `1`s), return the index of the row with the most `1`s. If several rows tie, return the smallest index. If there are no `1`s, return `-1`.

problems.title: Find Peak Element II
problems.statementMd:
A **peak** in a 2D grid is a cell strictly greater than its up, down, left and right neighbours (cells outside the grid count as `-1`).

Given an `n x m` grid `mat` of distinct non-negative values that has **exactly one** peak, return its position as `[row, col]`. Aim for `O(n log m)`.
constraints: values are distinct and there is exactly one peak

problems.title: Matrix Median
problems.statementMd: Given an `n x m` matrix whose rows are each sorted in non-decreasing order and where `n * m` is odd, return the median of all its elements, without flattening and sorting the matrix.

problems.title: Remove Outermost Parentheses
problems.statementMd:
A valid parentheses string splits uniquely into **primitive** parts: non-empty valid strings that can't be split further, like `(()())` or `()`.

Given a valid parentheses string `s`, remove the outermost pair of parentheses of every primitive part and return the result.
constraints: s is a valid parentheses string

problems.title: Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses
problems.statementMd: Given a valid expression `s` made of digits, `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and parentheses, return its **nesting depth**: the largest number of parentheses open at the same time.
constraints: the parentheses in s are balanced

problems.title: Count Substrings with Exactly K Distinct Characters
problems.statementMd: Given a lowercase string `s` and an integer `k`, return the number of substrings that contain **exactly** `k` distinct characters.

problems.title: Sum of Beauty of All Substrings
problems.statementMd:
The **beauty** of a string is the frequency of its most frequent character minus the frequency of its least frequent character (only counting characters that appear).

Given a lowercase string `s`, return the sum of the beauty of all its substrings.

problems.title: Reverse a Stack
problems.statementMd: A stack is given as an array `stack` whose **last** element is the top. Reverse the stack **in place** using recursion, using only stack operations (`push`, `pop`, checking whether it's empty). Don't return anything.

problems.title: Check if a Subsequence with Sum K Exists
problems.statementMd: Given an array of positive integers `nums` and an integer `k`, return `true` if some non-empty subsequence of `nums` sums to exactly `k`, otherwise `false`.

problems.title: Count Subsequences with Sum K
problems.statementMd: Given an array of positive integers `nums` and an integer `k`, return how many subsequences (chosen by index, so equal values count separately) sum to exactly `k`.

problems.title: Binary Strings Without Consecutive 1s
problems.statementMd: Given `n`, return every binary string of length `n` that has no two adjacent `1`s, in lexicographic (sorted) order.

problems.title: Rat in a Maze
problems.statementMd:
A rat starts at the top-left cell of an `n x n` grid and wants to reach the bottom-right cell. Cells with `1` are open and cells with `0` are blocked. It can move `D` (down), `L` (left), `R` (right) or `U` (up), and it can't visit a cell twice on the same path.

Return every path as a string of moves, sorted lexicographically. Return an empty array if the start or the destination is blocked or no path exists.

problems.title: M-Coloring Problem
problems.statementMd: Given an undirected graph with `n` vertices (`0` to `n - 1`) as an edge list and an integer `m`, return `true` if the vertices can be coloured with at most `m` colours so that no edge joins two vertices of the same colour.

problems.title: Check if the i-th Bit Is Set
problems.statementMd: Given a non-negative integer `n` and a bit index `i` (0 is the least significant bit), return `true` if bit `i` of `n` is `1`.

problems.title: Check if a Number Is Odd
problems.statementMd: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return `true` if it is odd, using a bitwise operation instead of `%`.

problems.title: Set the Rightmost Unset Bit
problems.statementMd: Given a positive integer `n`, set the rightmost `0` bit in its binary representation and return the result. If every bit of `n` is already `1` (like `7 = 111`), return `n` unchanged.

problems.title: Swap Two Numbers with XOR
problems.statementMd: Given two integers `a` and `b`, swap them **without a temporary variable** using XOR, and return `[a, b]` after the swap.

problems.title: XOR of Numbers in a Range
problems.statementMd: Given two integers `l <= r`, return `l ^ (l + 1) ^ ... ^ r` in `O(1)` time.

problems.title: Fractional Knapsack
problems.statementMd: Item `i` has value `val[i]` and weight `wt[i]`. You may take any fraction of an item. Return the largest total value that fits in a knapsack of capacity `capacity`, rounded to 2 decimal places (as a number).

problems.title: Shortest Job First
problems.statementMd:
All processes arrive at time `0` with burst times `bt`. A single CPU runs them one at a time with the **shortest job first** policy. A process's waiting time is when it starts running.

Return the average waiting time, rounded **down** to an integer.

problems.title: Job Sequencing Problem
problems.statementMd:
Each job is `[id, deadline, profit]`. Every job takes one unit of time, only one job runs at a time, and a job earns its profit only if it finishes by its deadline.

Return `[jobsDone, maxProfit]`: the most profit you can earn and how many jobs that schedule uses.

problems.title: N Meetings in One Room
problems.statementMd:
Meeting `i` runs from `start[i]` to `end[i]`. One room can host one meeting at a time, and a meeting can only begin **strictly after** the previous one ends.

Return the largest number of meetings the room can host.

problems.title: Minimum Platforms
problems.statementMd:
Train `i` arrives at `arr[i]` and departs at `dep[i]` (times as minutes in a day). A platform can't hold two trains at the same moment, and a train arriving at the exact minute another departs still needs its own platform.

Return the minimum number of platforms needed.

problems.title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
problems.statementMd: Given a lowercase string `s` and an integer `k`, return the length of the longest substring that contains at most `k` distinct characters.

problems.title: Minimum Window Subsequence
problems.statementMd: Given strings `s1` and `s2`, return the shortest contiguous substring `w` of `s1` such that `s2` is a subsequence of `w`. If several have the same length, return the one that starts first. Return `""` if there is none.

problems.title: Traversal in a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list, return the values of its nodes from head to tail as an array.

problems.title: Delete the Tail of a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list, delete its last node and return the head. Deleting from a one-node list leaves an empty list (`null`).

problems.title: Delete the K-th Node of a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list and an integer `k` (1-based), delete the `k`-th node and return the head. If the list has fewer than `k` nodes, return it unchanged.

problems.title: Delete the Node with Value X
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list and a value `x`, delete the **first** node whose value is `x` and return the head. If no node holds `x`, return the list unchanged.

problems.title: Insert at the Head of a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list (possibly empty) and a value `x`, insert a new node holding `x` at the front and return the new head.

problems.title: Insert at the Tail of a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list (possibly empty) and a value `x`, append a new node holding `x` at the end and return the head.

problems.title: Insert at the K-th Position of a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list, a value `x` and a position `k` (1-based, from `1` to `length + 1`), insert a new node holding `x` so that it becomes the `k`-th node. Return the head.

problems.title: Insert Before the Value X in a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list and two values `val` and `x`, insert a new node holding `val` right before the **first** node whose value is `x`. If no node holds `x`, return the list unchanged. Return the head.

problems.title: Length of a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list, return the number of nodes in it.

problems.title: Search in a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a singly linked list and a value `key`, return `true` if some node holds `key`, otherwise `false`.

problems.title: Sort a Linked List of 0s, 1s and 2s
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a linked list whose values are only `0`, `1` and `2`, rearrange it so all `0`s come first, then the `1`s, then the `2`s. Relink the nodes rather than creating new ones, and return the head.

problems.title: Add One to a Number Represented as a Linked List
problems.statementMd: A non-negative integer is stored in a linked list, one digit per node, **most significant digit first**, with no leading zeros (except the number `0` itself). Add one to it and return the head of the result.

problems.title: Length of Loop in a Linked List
problems.statementMd:
Given the `head` of a linked list that may contain a cycle, return the number of nodes in the cycle, or `0` if there is no cycle.

In the examples the list is shown as `{ list, pos }`: `pos` is the index the tail links back to, and `-1` means no cycle.

problems.title: Convert an Array to a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given an array `arr`, build a doubly linked list with the same values in order and return its head. Every node needs a correct `next` and `prev` (`prev` is `null` on the head). Create nodes with `new ListNode(val)` and set `prev` yourself.

problems.title: Delete the Tail of a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a non-empty doubly linked list, delete its last node and return the head (or `null` if the list becomes empty). Keep every `prev` pointer correct.

problems.title: Delete the K-th Node of a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a non-empty doubly linked list and `k` (1-based, `1 <= k <= length`), delete the `k`-th node and return the head. Keep every `prev` pointer correct.

problems.title: Remove a Given Node from a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a doubly linked list with **distinct** values and a value `x` that is in the list, remove the node holding `x` and return the head. Keep every `prev` pointer correct.
constraints: values are distinct and x is present

problems.title: Insert Before the Head of a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a doubly linked list (possibly empty) and a value `x`, insert a new node holding `x` before the head and return the new head. Keep every `prev` pointer correct.

problems.title: Insert Before the Tail of a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a non-empty doubly linked list and a value `x`, insert a new node holding `x` just before the last node and return the head. If the list has one node, the new node becomes the head.

problems.title: Insert Before the K-th Node of a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a non-empty doubly linked list, a position `k` (1-based, `1 <= k <= length`) and a value `x`, insert a new node holding `x` just before the `k`-th node and return the head.

problems.title: Insert Before a Given Node in a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a doubly linked list with **distinct** values, a value `target` that is in the list and a value `x`, insert a new node holding `x` just before the node holding `target`. Return the head.
constraints: values are distinct and target is present

problems.title: Delete the Head of a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a non-empty doubly linked list, delete the head node and return the new head (or `null`). The new head's `prev` must be `null`.

problems.title: Delete All Occurrences of a Key in a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a doubly linked list and a value `key`, delete every node holding `key` and return the head (or `null`). Keep every `prev` pointer correct.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from a Sorted Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a doubly linked list sorted in non-decreasing order, remove duplicate values so each value appears once, and return the head. Keep every `prev` pointer correct.

problems.title: Pairs with a Given Sum in a Sorted Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a sorted doubly linked list of **distinct** positive integers and a `target`, return every pair `[a, b]` with `a < b` and `a + b == target`, ordered by `a` ascending.

problems.title: Implement a Stack Using an Array
problems.statementMd:
Implement `ArrayStack` on top of a plain array and a top index (don't rely on `push`/`pop` doing the work for you):

- `push(x)` adds `x` on top.
- `pop()` removes and returns the top, or `-1` if the stack is empty.
- `top()` returns the top without removing it, or `-1`.
- `isEmpty()` returns whether the stack is empty.

The judge drives your class through `runOps(ops)`: each operation is `[method, ...args]`, and the answer is the list of values the calls return (`null` for methods that return nothing).

problems.title: Implement a Queue Using an Array
problems.statementMd:
Implement `ArrayQueue` with an array and front/rear indexes (avoid `shift`, which is O(n)):

- `push(x)` adds `x` at the back.
- `pop()` removes and returns the front, or `-1` if the queue is empty.
- `peek()` returns the front without removing it, or `-1`.
- `isEmpty()` returns whether the queue is empty.

The judge drives your class through `runOps(ops)`: each operation is `[method, ...args]`, and the answer is the list of values the calls return (`null` for methods that return nothing).

problems.title: Implement a Stack Using a Linked List
problems.statementMd:
Implement `LinkedListStack` using linked nodes (`{ val, next }`), not an array:

- `push(x)` adds `x` on top.
- `pop()` removes and returns the top, or `-1` if the stack is empty.
- `top()` returns the top without removing it, or `-1`.
- `isEmpty()` returns whether the stack is empty.

The judge drives your class through `runOps(ops)`: each operation is `[method, ...args]`, and the answer is the list of values the calls return (`null` for methods that return nothing).

problems.title: Implement a Queue Using a Linked List
problems.statementMd:
Implement `LinkedListQueue` using linked nodes (`{ val, next }`), not an array:

- `push(x)` adds `x` at the back.
- `pop()` removes and returns the front, or `-1` if the queue is empty.
- `peek()` returns the front without removing it, or `-1`.
- `isEmpty()` returns whether the queue is empty.

The judge drives your class through `runOps(ops)`: each operation is `[method, ...args]`, and the answer is the list of values the calls return (`null` for methods that return nothing).

problems.title: Infix to Postfix
problems.statementMd:
Given a valid infix expression `s`, convert it to postfix and return it.

Operands are single letters. Operators are `+ - * / ^`: `^` binds tightest and groups right to left, `*` and `/` come next, `+` and `-` bind loosest, and all except `^` group left to right. Infix input may contain parentheses; the output has none and no spaces.

problems.title: Infix to Prefix
problems.statementMd:
Given a valid infix expression `s`, convert it to prefix and return it.

Operands are single letters. Operators are `+ - * / ^`: `^` binds tightest and groups right to left, `*` and `/` come next, `+` and `-` bind loosest, and all except `^` group left to right. Infix input may contain parentheses; the output has none and no spaces.

problems.title: Prefix to Infix
problems.statementMd:
Given a valid prefix expression `s`, convert it to fully parenthesised infix and return it.

Operands are single letters. Operators are `+ - * / ^`: `^` binds tightest and groups right to left, `*` and `/` come next, `+` and `-` bind loosest, and all except `^` group left to right. Wrap every operator with its two operands in parentheses, e.g. `(A+B)`, with no spaces.

problems.title: Prefix to Postfix
problems.statementMd:
Given a valid prefix expression `s`, convert it to postfix and return it.

Operands are single letters. Operators are `+ - * / ^`: `^` binds tightest and groups right to left, `*` and `/` come next, `+` and `-` bind loosest, and all except `^` group left to right. The output has no spaces.

problems.title: Postfix to Infix
problems.statementMd:
Given a valid postfix expression `s`, convert it to fully parenthesised infix and return it.

Operands are single letters. Operators are `+ - * / ^`: `^` binds tightest and groups right to left, `*` and `/` come next, `+` and `-` bind loosest, and all except `^` group left to right. Wrap every operator with its two operands in parentheses, e.g. `(A+B)`, with no spaces.

problems.title: Postfix to Prefix
problems.statementMd:
Given a valid postfix expression `s`, convert it to prefix and return it.

Operands are single letters. Operators are `+ - * / ^`: `^` binds tightest and groups right to left, `*` and `/` come next, `+` and `-` bind loosest, and all except `^` group left to right. The output has no spaces.

problems.title: Next Smaller Element
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array where position `i` holds the first element to the **right** of `nums[i]` that is strictly smaller than it, or `-1` if there is none.

problems.title: Number of Greater Elements to the Right
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and a list of query `indices`, return for each query index `i` how many elements to the right of `nums[i]` are strictly greater than it.

problems.title: The Celebrity Problem
problems.statementMd: At a party of `n` people, `M[i][j] = 1` means person `i` knows person `j` (`M[i][i]` is always `0`). A **celebrity** is known by everyone else and knows no one. Return the celebrity's index, or `-1` if there is none.

problems.title: Heapify Algorithm
problems.statementMd:
`nums` is a valid **min-heap** stored as an array (children of `i` are `2i + 1` and `2i + 2`). Set `nums[ind] = val`, then restore the heap property **in place**:

- If the new value is smaller than its parent, sift it **up** by swapping with the parent while it's smaller.
- Otherwise sift it **down**: while it's larger than its smaller child, swap with that child (the left child on a tie).

Don't return anything.

problems.title: Build a Min-Heap from an Array
problems.statementMd: Turn `nums` into a **min-heap in place** with the bottom-up method: for `i` from `floor(n / 2) - 1` down to `0`, sift `nums[i]` down (swap with its smaller child, the left one on a tie, while that child is smaller). Return the array.

problems.title: Implement a Min-Heap
problems.statementMd:
Implement `MinHeap` with an array (no sorting):

- `insert(x)` adds `x`.
- `getMin()` returns the smallest value, or `-1` if the heap is empty.
- `extractMin()` removes and returns the smallest value, or `-1`.
- `heapSize()` returns the number of values.

The judge drives your class through `runOps(ops)`: each operation is `[method, ...args]`, and the answer is the list of values the calls return (`null` for methods that return nothing).

problems.title: Implement a Max-Heap
problems.statementMd:
Implement `MaxHeap` with an array (no sorting):

- `insert(x)` adds `x`.
- `getMax()` returns the largest value, or `-1` if the heap is empty.
- `extractMax()` removes and returns the largest value, or `-1`.
- `heapSize()` returns the number of values.

The judge drives your class through `runOps(ops)`: each operation is `[method, ...args]`, and the answer is the list of values the calls return (`null` for methods that return nothing).

problems.title: Check if an Array Is a Min-Heap
problems.statementMd: Given an array `nums`, return `true` if it represents a **min-heap**: every element is `<=` its children at indexes `2i + 1` and `2i + 2` (when they exist).

problems.title: Convert a Min-Heap to a Max-Heap
problems.statementMd: Given a min-heap `nums`, convert it **in place** to a max-heap with the bottom-up method: for `i` from `floor(n / 2) - 1` down to `0`, sift `nums[i]` down toward its **larger** child (the left one on a tie) while that child is larger. Return the array.

problems.title: Heap Sort
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, sort it in non-decreasing order with **heap sort** and return it: build a max heap in the array, then repeatedly swap the root (the maximum) to the end and sift the new root down within the shrinking heap.

problems.title: Replace Elements by Their Rank
problems.statementMd: Replace every element of `nums` by its **rank**: the smallest value gets rank `1`, equal values share a rank, and ranks have no gaps. Return the new array.

problems.title: Minimum Cost to Connect Sticks
problems.statementMd: You can join two sticks of lengths `x` and `y` into one stick of length `x + y` at a cost of `x + y`. Join all `sticks` into one and return the minimum total cost.

problems.title: Maximum Sum Combinations
problems.statementMd: Given two integer arrays `a` and `b` of the same length `n` and an integer `k`, consider all `n * n` sums `a[i] + b[j]`. Return the `k` largest sums in non-increasing order.

problems.title: Preorder, Inorder and Postorder in One Traversal
problems.statementMd: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return `[inorder, preorder, postorder]`: its three depth-first traversals, computed in **one** pass with a single stack.

problems.title: Children Sum Property
problems.statementMd: Return `true` if every node of the binary tree that has at least one child holds a value equal to the sum of its children's values (a missing child counts as `0`). Leaves and an empty tree satisfy the property.

problems.title: Boundary Traversal of a Binary Tree
problems.statementMd:
Return the boundary of the binary tree, anticlockwise from the root:

1. The root (once).
2. The **left boundary** top-down: start at `root.left` and keep going left (or right when there's no left child), excluding leaves.
3. All **leaves** from left to right.
4. The **right boundary** bottom-up: start at `root.right`, keep going right (or left), excluding leaves.

A single-node tree's boundary is just the root.

problems.title: Top View of a Binary Tree
problems.statementMd: Return the **top view** of the binary tree: for each vertical column from left to right, the node seen first when looking down. The root is in column `0`, a left child is one column left of its parent and a right child one column right. When several nodes share a column, take the one at the smallest depth; on a tie, the one met first in level order (left to right).

problems.title: Bottom View of a Binary Tree
problems.statementMd: Return the **bottom view** of the binary tree: for each vertical column from left to right, the node seen when looking up from below. The root is in column `0`, a left child is one column left of its parent and a right child one column right. When several nodes share a column, take the deepest; on a tie, the one met **last** in level order.

problems.title: All Root-to-Leaf Paths
problems.statementMd: Return every path from the root to a leaf of the binary tree, as lists of node values, ordered from the leftmost leaf to the rightmost.

problems.title: Minimum Time to Burn a Binary Tree
problems.statementMd: A fire starts at the node whose value is `start` (all values are distinct). Every second the fire spreads from each burning node to its parent and children. Return the number of seconds until the whole tree is burning.
constraints: start is a value in the tree

problems.title: Traversals Needed for a Unique Binary Tree
problems.statementMd: Traversals are coded `1` = preorder, `2` = inorder, `3` = postorder. Given two codes `a` and `b`, return `true` if those two traversals together always identify a unique binary tree (assuming distinct values).

problems.title: Floor and Ceil in a BST
problems.statementMd: Given the `root` of a binary search tree with distinct values and an integer `key`, return `[floor, ceil]`: the largest value `<= key` and the smallest value `>= key`. Use `-1` for either if it doesn't exist.

problems.title: Minimum and Maximum in a BST
problems.statementMd: Given the `root` of a non-empty binary search tree, return `[min, max]`: its smallest and largest values.

problems.title: Inorder Predecessor and Successor in a BST
problems.statementMd: Given the `root` of a binary search tree with distinct values and a `key` (which may or may not be in the tree), return `[predecessor, successor]`: the largest value strictly less than `key` and the smallest value strictly greater than `key`. Use `-1` when one doesn't exist.

problems.title: Largest BST in a Binary Tree
problems.statementMd: Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the number of nodes in its largest subtree that is a binary search tree (every node strictly greater than everything in its left subtree and strictly smaller than everything in its right subtree). A subtree means a node with **all** its descendants. An empty tree has answer `0`.

problems.title: BFS and DFS of a Graph
problems.statementMd: Given an undirected graph with `V` vertices as an adjacency list `adj` (`adj[u]` lists the neighbours of `u`, in the order they must be explored), return `[bfs, dfs]`: the breadth-first and the recursive depth-first visiting orders starting from vertex `0`. Only vertices reachable from `0` appear.

problems.title: Number of Connected Components
problems.statementMd: Given `V` vertices numbered `0` to `V - 1` and a list of undirected `edges`, return the number of connected components.

problems.title: Number of Distinct Islands
problems.statementMd: Given a grid of `0`s (water) and `1`s (land), an island is a group of land cells connected up, down, left or right. Two islands are the same if one can be **translated** (not rotated or reflected) to match the other. Return the number of distinct islands.

problems.title: Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm)
problems.statementMd: Given a directed acyclic graph with `V` vertices and directed `edges` (`[u, v]` means `u` must come before `v`), return a topological order. Several orders may be valid: return the **lexicographically smallest** one (always take the smallest available vertex).

problems.title: Alien Dictionary
problems.statementMd: An alien language uses the first `k` letters of the English alphabet in an unknown order. `words` is sorted by that order. Return the order of the `k` letters as a string. Several orders may fit: return the **lexicographically smallest** one (when several letters are free, take the earliest in the English alphabet). The input is always consistent.

problems.title: Shortest Path in a Weighted DAG
problems.statementMd: Given a directed acyclic graph with `V` vertices and weighted `edges` (`[u, v, w]` is an edge from `u` to `v` of weight `w`), return the shortest distance from vertex `0` to every vertex, using `-1` for vertices that can't be reached.

problems.title: Shortest Path with Unit Weights
problems.statementMd: Given an undirected graph with `V` vertices, unweighted `edges` and a source `src`, return the minimum number of edges from `src` to every vertex, using `-1` for vertices that can't be reached.

problems.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
problems.statementMd: Given an undirected graph with `V` vertices, weighted `edges` (`[u, v, w]`, `w >= 0`) and a source `src`, return the shortest distance from `src` to every vertex, using `-1` for vertices that can't be reached.

problems.title: Print the Shortest Path
problems.statementMd: Given an undirected weighted graph with vertices `1` to `n` and `edges` (`[u, v, w]`), return the vertices of the shortest path from `1` to `n`, in order. Every weight is a different power of two, so the shortest path is unique. Return `[-1]` if `n` can't be reached.

problems.title: Minimum Multiplications to Reach End
problems.statementMd: Starting from `start`, one step multiplies the current number by any value in `arr` and takes the result modulo `100000`. Return the minimum number of steps to reach `end`, or `-1` if it's impossible.

problems.title: Bellman-Ford Algorithm
problems.statementMd: Given a directed graph with `V` vertices, weighted `edges` (`[u, v, w]`, `w` may be negative) and a source `src`, return the shortest distance from `src` to every vertex, using `100000000` for vertices that can't be reached. If a negative-weight cycle is reachable from `src`, return `[-1]`.

problems.title: Floyd-Warshall Algorithm
problems.statementMd: `matrix[i][j]` is the weight of the directed edge from `i` to `j` (non-negative), or `-1` if there is no edge; the diagonal is `0`. Return the matrix of shortest distances between every pair, with `-1` where `j` can't be reached from `i`.

problems.title: Disjoint Set (Union-Find)
problems.statementMd:
Implement `DisjointSet` over non-negative integer elements, each starting in its own set:

- `unionSets(u, v)` merges the sets containing `u` and `v`.
- `connected(u, v)` returns whether `u` and `v` are in the same set.

Use union by size (or rank) and path compression.

The judge drives your class through `runOps(ops)`: each operation is `[method, ...args]`, and the answer is the list of values the calls return (`null` for methods that return nothing).

problems.title: Minimum Spanning Tree Weight
problems.statementMd: Given a connected undirected graph with `V` vertices and weighted `edges` (`[u, v, w]`), return the total weight of a minimum spanning tree.

problems.title: Number of Islands II
problems.statementMd: An `n x m` grid starts as all water. Each operation `[r, c]` turns that cell into land (it may already be land). After every operation, report the number of islands (groups of land cells connected up, down, left or right). Return the list of counts.

problems.title: Articulation Points
problems.statementMd: Given an undirected graph with `V` vertices and `edges`, return every **articulation point** (a vertex whose removal increases the number of connected components) in increasing order, or `[-1]` if there are none.

problems.title: Frog Jump
problems.statementMd: A frog starts on stair `0` and wants to reach the last stair. From stair `i` it can jump to `i + 1` or `i + 2`, and a jump from `i` to `j` costs `|heights[i] - heights[j]|` energy. Return the minimum total energy.

problems.title: Frog Jump with K Distances
problems.statementMd: Like Frog Jump, but from stair `i` the frog can jump to any of `i + 1, ..., i + k`. A jump from `i` to `j` costs `|heights[i] - heights[j]|`. Return the minimum total energy to reach the last stair from stair `0`.

problems.title: Ninja's Training
problems.statementMd: A ninja trains for `n` days. Each day they pick one of three activities, and `points[i][j]` is the merit for doing activity `j` on day `i`. They can't do the same activity two days in a row. Return the maximum total merit.

problems.title: Subset Sum Equal to Target
problems.statementMd: Given an array of non-negative integers `arr` and an integer `target`, return `true` if some subset of `arr` (possibly empty) sums to exactly `target`.

problems.title: Count Subsets with Sum K
problems.statementMd: Given an array of non-negative integers `arr` and an integer `k`, return the number of subsets (chosen by index, so equal values at different positions count separately) whose sum is `k`, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

problems.title: Count Partitions with Given Difference
problems.statementMd: Split `arr` (non-negative integers) into two subsets `S1` and `S2` (every element in exactly one, chosen by index) so that `sum(S1) - sum(S2) = diff` and `sum(S1) >= sum(S2)`. Return the number of ways modulo `10^9 + 7`.

problems.title: 0/1 Knapsack
problems.statementMd: Item `i` has weight `wt[i]` and value `val[i]`. Choose items, each **at most once**, with total weight at most `W`, to maximise the total value. Return that value.

problems.title: Unbounded Knapsack
problems.statementMd: Item `i` has weight `wt[i]` and value `val[i]`, and you may take **any number of copies** of each item. With total weight at most `W`, return the maximum total value.

problems.title: Rod Cutting
problems.statementMd: A rod has length `n = price.length`, and a piece of length `i + 1` sells for `price[i]`. Cut the rod into pieces (or not at all) to maximise the total selling price. Return that maximum.

problems.title: Print the Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.statementMd: Return a longest **strictly increasing** subsequence of `nums` (the values, in order). If several exist, return the one whose list of chosen **indexes** is lexicographically smallest.

problems.title: Longest Bitonic Subsequence
problems.statementMd: A subsequence is **bitonic** if it strictly increases and then strictly decreases. Either part may be empty, so a purely increasing or purely decreasing subsequence counts too. Return the length of the longest bitonic subsequence of `nums`.

problems.title: Longest Common Substring
problems.statementMd: Return the length of the longest string that is a **contiguous** substring of both `s1` and `s2`.

problems.title: Count Palindromic Subsequences
problems.statementMd: Return the number of non-empty palindromic subsequences of `s`, counted by the positions chosen (so equal strings picked from different positions count separately), modulo `10^9 + 7`.

problems.title: Matrix Chain Multiplication
problems.statementMd: Matrix `i` (1-based, `i = 1..n-1`) has dimensions `dims[i-1] x dims[i]`. Multiplying a `p x q` matrix by a `q x r` matrix costs `p * q * r`. Return the minimum total cost to multiply the whole chain.

problems.title: Evaluate Boolean Expression to True
problems.statementMd: `s` alternates operands `T` / `F` and operators `&`, `|`, `^` (e.g. `T|F&T`). Return the number of ways to fully parenthesise it so that it evaluates to `true`, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

problems.title: Implement Trie II (Counts and Erase)
problems.statementMd:
Implement `Trie` for lowercase words, where the same word can be inserted several times:

- `insert(word)` adds one copy of `word`.
- `countWordsEqualTo(word)` returns how many copies of `word` are stored.
- `countWordsStartingWith(prefix)` returns how many stored words (counting copies) start with `prefix`.
- `erase(word)` removes one copy of `word` if there is one.

The judge drives your class through `runOps(ops)`: each operation is `[method, ...args]`, and the answer is the list of values the calls return (`null` for methods that return nothing).

problems.title: Longest Word with All Prefixes
problems.statementMd: Return the longest string in `words` such that **every** prefix of it (including the full word) is also in `words`. On a tie in length, return the lexicographically smallest. If no word qualifies, return `"None"`.

problems.title: Number of Distinct Substrings
problems.statementMd: Return the number of distinct **non-empty** substrings of `s`.

problems.title: Rabin-Karp Pattern Search
problems.statementMd: Return every 0-based index where `pattern` occurs in `text` (occurrences may overlap), in increasing order. Aim for a rolling hash (Rabin-Karp).

problems.title: Z-Function
problems.statementMd: Return the **Z-array** of `s`: `z[i]` is the length of the longest substring starting at `i` that is also a prefix of `s`. By convention `z[0] = 0`. Aim for O(n).

problems.title: KMP: Build the LPS Array
problems.statementMd: Return the **LPS array** of `s` used by the KMP algorithm: `lps[i]` is the length of the longest proper prefix of `s[0..i]` that is also a suffix of `s[0..i]`. Aim for O(n).

problems.title: All Primes up to N
problems.statementMd: Return every prime number `<= n` in increasing order. Aim for the Sieve of Eratosthenes.

problems.title: Prime Factorisation
problems.statementMd: Return the prime factorisation of `n` as a list of primes in increasing order, each repeated as many times as it divides `n`. For `n = 1` return an empty list.

problems.title: Count Vowels
problems.statementMd:
Given a string `s`, return how many of its characters are vowels.

The vowels are `a`, `e`, `i`, `o` and `u`, in either lowercase or uppercase. Every other character (consonants, digits, spaces, punctuation) does not count.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters

problems.title: Reverse a String
problems.statementMd:
Given a string `s`, return a new string with its characters in reverse order.

Build the result with a loop instead of `split().reverse().join()`.

problems.title: Check if a String is a Palindrome
problems.statementMd:
Given a string `s`, return `true` if it reads exactly the same forwards and backwards, otherwise `false`.

Compare characters as they are: case, spaces and punctuation all matter here (`"Aa"` is not a palindrome).

problems.title: Count Occurrences of a Character
problems.statementMd: Given a string `s` and a single character `c`, return how many times `c` appears in `s`. The match is case-sensitive.

problems.title: Convert to Uppercase
problems.statementMd:
Given a string `s`, return it with every lowercase English letter (`a`-`z`) turned into its uppercase form. Every other character stays as it is.

Do it with character codes (`charCodeAt` / `String.fromCharCode`) instead of `toUpperCase()`.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters

problems.title: Count Words in a Sentence
problems.statementMd:
Given a string `s` made of letters and spaces, return the number of words in it. A word is a maximal run of non-space characters.

Words can be separated by more than one space, and `s` can start or end with spaces.
constraints: s consists of English letters and spaces

problems.title: First Unique Character in a String
Count Distinct Elements
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums`, return how many **different** values it contains.

problems.title: Most Frequent Element
problems.statementMd: Given a non-empty integer array `nums`, return the value that appears most often. If several values share the highest count, return the **smallest** of them.

problems.title: Check if Two Arrays Hold the Same Values
problems.statementMd: Given two integer arrays `a` and `b`, return `true` if they contain exactly the same values with the same counts (in any order), otherwise `false`.

problems.title: Count Pairs with Given Sum
problems.statementMd: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the number of index pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` and `nums[i] + nums[j] == k`.

problems.title: Print 1 to N Using Recursion
problems.statementMd: Given a positive integer `n`, return the list `[1, 2, ..., n]`. Build it **recursively**: no loops.

problems.title: Print N to 1 Using Recursion
problems.statementMd: Given a positive integer `n`, return the list `[n, n - 1, ..., 1]`. Build it **recursively**: no loops.

problems.title: Sort a Stack Using Recursion
problems.statementMd:
A stack is given as an array `stack`, bottom first (the last element is the top).

Sort it so the **largest** value is on top, and return it in the same bottom-first form. Use recursion and only stack operations (push, pop, peek); no sorting helpers and no extra array.

problems.title: Find the Winner of the Circular Game
Reverse a Doubly Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a doubly linked list, reverse it and return the new head. Every node must end up with correct `next` and `prev` pointers (`prev` is `null` on the new head).

problems.title: Find the Starting Point of a Loop in a Linked List
problems.statementMd:
Given the `head` of a linked list that may contain a loop, return the **0-based position** of the node where the loop begins, or `-1` if there is no loop.

In the examples the list is shown as `{ list, pos }`: `pos` is the index the tail links back to, and `-1` means no loop. Your function only receives `head`.
constraints: Use O(1) extra memory for the follow-up

problems.title: Delete the Head of a Linked List
problems.statementMd: Given the `head` of a non-empty singly linked list, delete the first node and return the new head (`null` if the list becomes empty).
